claims.text: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, its SystemOne model, in the week before this post (September 2026).
TypeSafe's Jev provides AI primitives that let apps, agents, and workflows make decisions based on context.
Jev's decision-making primitives are confidence scoring, multiple choice, and yes/no (noul) questions.
GeoDeploy compares every AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud region that offers managed Kubernetes and provisions consistent environments across all three hyperscalers.

In GeoDeploy, the TypeScript app takes the request, fetches live pricing and does all math; Jev decides region and modules and never does arithmetic, generates code, or invents region names; Pulumi provisions clusters, registries, workloads, and DNS.
GeoDeploy uses great-circle distance as a coverage measure across candidate regions.
GeoDeploy fetches current prices from the AWS Price List API, the Azure Retail Prices API, and the Google Cloud Billing Catalog, normalized into a single quote format.
GeoDeploy's deterministic TypeScript bin-packs pods onto nodes, filters out instance types not matching the image's architecture, and computes a monthly cost per candidate.
GeoDeploy composes Pulumi programs from a registry of typed modules: EKS, AKS, or GKE; ECR, ACR, or Artifact Registry; ingress; DNS through Route 53, NS1, or Cloudflare; and observability.
GeoDeploy uses the Pulumi Automation API to run a preview and then an update, with one stack per region, and will not run unless cloud credentials pass readiness checks.
Every GeoDeploy run writes plan.json and plan.md with the full decision record, and a web UI shows the deployment on a live globe.

Jev returns typed answers with calibrated confidence through three primitives: choice() picks one option from a closed list and returns the pick, a probability distribution across options, and a confidence; score() rates against a rubric (GeoDeploy uses 10 levels); noul() answers a yes/no question with a single probability.
Jev only selects from closed sets and never writes code or does arithmetic, so a hallucinated region or made-up Pulumi argument cannot happen by construction.
For each geo, GeoDeploy sends Jev a shortlist of up to 40 priced candidates in a single call.
GeoDeploy asks Jev for a selection, five quality scores (coverage, cost fit, maturity, sprawl risk, architecture consistency), two hard noul checks (residency, capacity), and a fallback region.
The file packages/decide/src/questions.ts in GeoDeploy imports choice, noul, and score from @typesafe-ai/sdk.
TypeSafe's advice for rubrics is to "describe situations, not degrees."
The TypeSafeClient exposes a systemOne method taking state and questions and returning answers with fields such as selection.choice, selection.confidence, residencyOk.noul, coverage.score.
GeoDeploy's ranking uses weight profiles: latency-optimized (default), balanced, residency-first, and failure-domain.
The latency-optimized profile weights are cost 0.13, coverage 0.48, maturity 0.17, sprawl 0.1, archConsistency 0.12, and other profiles have the listed weights.
In GeoDeploy, cluster and registry modules follow from the provider, and Jev decides ingress posture, autoscaling posture, and node-pool sizing tier.

GeoDeploy confidence thresholds: data residency 0.95 (hard reject); new-cluster region 0.90 (top three flagged for human); existing-stack region 0.75 (keep existing region); ingress/autoscaling module 0.85 (registry default); node-pool sizing 0.60 (bin-packing result); global floor 0.50 (drop AI path for that geo).
Each AiPathAborted in GeoDeploy carries the full attempt (state, questions, and answers).

If a gate check fails, the API times out or errors, or upstream is unreachable, GeoDeploy switches to a deterministic fallback comparing prices across providers while enforcing residency and constraint checks.
Running `geodeploy explain` shows why each region won.

In GeoDeploy self-driving mode (`geodeploy monitor`), the agent periodically checks CPU utilization and asks Jev one joint question across regions with options no-change, scale-up:<geo>, scale-down:<geo>, or shift:<from>-><to>, plus a disruption-risk check; code computes node-count changes.

In self-driving mode, above 0.85 confidence the resize is applied automatically; between 0.70 and 0.85 it is suggested for human approval; below 0.70 GeoDeploy ignores Jev's pick and uses a deterministic per-region rule based on utilization.
CPU utilization alone makes a poor autoscaling metric and is usually paired with other signals such as request latency and error rates.
GeoDeploy is released as open source at github.com/pulumi/devx-geodeploy.
The Pulumi Automation API page exists at /automation/.
